phases.name: Member accept vertical plus issuance core

steps.name: Walking skeleton: admin invites a teammate who creates an account and joins as a member
criteria: Greens exactly one scenario: "An admin invites a teammate who creates an account and joins as a member".

An admin GETs /workspace/invites, POSTs a teammate email, and gets a shareable signed /invites/accept link; the invitee with no account opens it, sets a policy-passing password, and is created and joined.

The new code is built in this step: Store::create_member_and_consume (ONE tx: guarded-UPDATE consume, INSERT user with argon2id hash, INSERT role='member' membership, set used_by, COMMIT; SQLSTATE-23505 collision-safe), the data-derived kind-dispatch arm in submit_accept, the invite_accept_view extension surfacing invitee_email plus created_by, and the /workspace/invites issuance route plus member_invites.rs handlers plus templates.
The invitee lands on the inviting workspace signed in with no separate login, invites.used_at is set exactly once, and exactly one user plus one member membership exist.

Genuinely RED by MISSING: no /workspace/invites route, no member_invites.rs handlers, no create_member_and_consume tx, and no member dispatch arm exist yet (route unknown / handler absent against real testcontainers PG16, never IMPORT_ERROR / FIXTURE_BROKEN).

Per D7/OD-C, run cargo xtask check-arch; add a LAYER-1e allow-list line for the issuance handler ONLY if the run flags member_invites.rs (provisional: no line, the handler scopes off session.workspace_id).
steps.scenario_name: An admin invites a teammate who creates an account and joins as a member

steps.name: Issuance happy paths: form, shareable link, email-fail-safe, second independent invite
criteria: Greens four scenarios: "An admin opens the member-invite form for her workspace", "Submitting a valid email creates an invite and shows a shareable link", "The shareable link is shown even when the invite email fails to send", and "An admin can issue a second independent invite to the same email".

An admin GET on /workspace/invites renders the one-email-field form naming her workspace; a valid POST inserts an invite via insert_invite (created_by = inviter) and renders the shareable signed link.
A best-effort email send failure is logged at warn and is non-fatal: the shareable link is still shown so the admin can paste it out-of-band (FR-2, AC-01.4).
Issuing a second invite to the same email creates an independent invite row (no collapse), proving insert_invite is reused as-is per D2 (BR-3).
Green-by-inheritance once the walking skeleton's issuance form template, submit_invite handler, and 'invite sent' fragment exist.
steps.scenario_name: An admin opens the member-invite form for her workspace

steps.name: Member accept GET plus immediate happy accepts including expiry-inside boundary
criteria: Greens four scenarios: "A live member invite renders a set-password form naming the workspace", "Opening the member-accept page creates no account and consumes nothing", "A near-fresh member invite accepts immediately", and "A member invite opened just inside its expiry window is accepted".

A GET on a live member invite renders the set-password form naming the workspace; the GET is non-committal, creating no account and consuming nothing (used_at still NULL), so only the POST consume tx is authoritative.

A near-fresh member invite POST completes immediately via create_member_and_consume, and an invite one second from expiring (just inside its window) also accepts, proving the in-tx expiry boundary is inclusive up to expires_at (AC-02.7, NFR-2).
Green-by-inheritance once the accept GET 'join as a member' copy, the invite_accept_view extension, and create_member_and_consume from the walking skeleton exist.
Pairs with the just-past-expiry refusal (02-01) to pin the NFR-2 expiry edge on the member arm.
steps.scenario_name: A live member invite renders a set-password form naming the workspace

steps.name: Member isolation plus role: lands on inviting workspace, cannot reach issuance
criteria: Greens two scenarios: "The new member lands on the inviting workspace and sees only its data" and "A newly joined member cannot reach the admin issuance surface".
The newly joined member lands on the inviting workspace (landed workspace_id == invites.workspace_id via resolve_active_workspace) and sees only that tenant's data (FR-6, AC-02.4).

The new member's membership is role='member', so a GET on /workspace/invites returns the byte-identical non-enumerable 404 (resource_not_found_page) the issuance admin gate produces (AC-02.6, BR-2, NFR-1).
Green-by-inheritance once the member arm mints the role='member' membership and the issuance is_workspace_admin gate exist.
steps.scenario_name: The new member lands on the inviting workspace and sees only its data

steps.name: First-admin regression guard: shipped accept path unchanged
criteria: Greens exactly one scenario: "A first-admin invite still routes to the shipped accept path" (@verify-path-unchanged).

A first-admin invite (consumer == created_by, account pre-exists) is dispatched to the SHIPPED set_first_admin_password_and_consume tx, not the new member arm; the shipped first-admin behavior is byte-identical.
The data-derived kind dispatch in submit_accept does not change the shipped first-admin path; the foundry-acceptance @all suite that was green-before stays green-after.
Green-by-inheritance once the kind dispatch routes the first-admin discriminator to the unchanged tx; this step is the regression litmus that re-REDs if the dispatch breaks the shipped flow.
steps.scenario_name: A first-admin invite still routes to the shipped accept path

phases.name: Security: refusal non-enumerability, single-use, CSRF, no-leak

steps.name: Expiry refusals: expired and just-past-window refused without leaking existence
criteria: Greens two scenarios: "An expired member invite is refused without leaking existence" and "A member invite opened just past its expiry window is refused".

An expired member invite returns the SHIPPED uniform invite_refusal_page() (200 OK) revealing nothing about whether any account or workspace exists; this is the canonical refusal arm 02-02 asserts byte-identity against (AC-03.2/03.3).

A member invite that expired one second ago (just outside its window) returns a response byte-identical (status and full body bytes) to the expired refusal, pinning the expiry edge on the refusal side (AC-03.4, NFR-2).
Green-by-inheritance once the accept GET liveness check wires the member invite to the shipped invite_refusal_page().
steps.scenario_name: An expired member invite is refused without leaking existence

steps.name: Refusal matrix plus byte-identity across all five invalid reasons
criteria: Greens three scenarios: "Accept refusals are byte-identical across all five invalid reasons" (@property), "A tampered signature is refused identically to an expired link", and "An unknown invite id is refused identically to every other reason".

A tampered signature fails HMAC verify before any DB hit and an unknown invite id are each refused with a response byte-identical (status and full body) to the expired refusal; the reason lives only in internal tracing keyed on invite_id (AC-03.2).

Expired, used, tampered, unknown, and email-collision links all produce one byte-identical user-visible refusal page; collapsing any two arms into divergent responses must re-RED this @property assertion (AC-03.2/03.3/03.8, NFR-3).
Green-by-inheritance once the five-arm uniform refusal (including the collision arm built in 02-03) is wired to the member accept.
steps.scenario_name: Accept refusals are byte-identical across all five invalid reasons

steps.name: Email-collision is non-enumerable: existing-account email refused, not a 500
criteria: Greens exactly one scenario: "A member invite whose email already has an account is refused without leaking that fact".

A member invite whose invitee_email already maps to an existing user triggers a users.email_lower UNIQUE violation (SQLSTATE 23505) caught INSIDE the tx, mapped to EmailCollision, and rendered as the uniform invite_refusal_page() (NOT a 500, no DB-constraint error leak) per D5/OD-1 and AC-03.8.
The collision is caught via the UNIQUE constraint, not a pre-check SELECT (race-safe, no enumeration oracle), and the invite is NOT consumed: the tx rolls back wholesale (BR-5, NFR-3).

Genuinely RED by MISSING the UNIQUE-violation-catch arm in create_member_and_consume; this is the highest-risk arm the DISCUSS flagged HIGH and must red for a REAL oracle (collision-500 or invite-consumed flags upstream-issues.md).
steps.scenario_name: A member invite whose email already has an account is refused without leaking that fact

steps.name: Single-use plus concurrency plus TOCTOU: account created exactly once
criteria: Greens three scenarios: "Concurrent accepts of one member invite create the account exactly once" (@property), "A consumed member invite can never be used again", and "A member invite consumed between opening the page and submitting is refused by the transaction guard".

Two concurrent accepts of one live member invite mean the atomic guarded UPDATE (not a read-then-write) lets exactly one create the user plus membership plus sign-in; the other gets the uniform refusal, and exactly one user, one membership, one consumed invite result (AC-03.6, NFR-2).
After a successful accept, re-opening the same member invite returns the uniform refusal with no second account and no second consume; the guarded UPDATE matches zero rows (AC-03.5).

A member invite consumed by another submission between opening the page and submitting is refused by the in-tx zero-rows guard, proving the GET liveness check is advisory and the tx guard re-checks liveness and expiry atomically (AC-03.7, TOCTOU closed).
Green-by-inheritance once create_member_and_consume's guarded-UPDATE-consume race-safety from the walking skeleton is exercised under concurrency and replay.
steps.scenario_name: Concurrent accepts of one member invite create the account exactly once

steps.name: Issuance authz non-enumerability: non-admin and signed-out cannot tell the surface exists
criteria: Greens two scenarios: "A non-admin cannot tell the issuance surface exists" and "A signed-out caller cannot tell the issuance surface exists" (@property).
A non-admin GET or POST to /workspace/invites is refused by the is_workspace_admin gate with the byte-identical non-enumerable 404 (resource_not_found_page) and creates no invite (AC-03.1, NFR-1).

A signed-out caller's GET or POST is refused byte-identically to the non-admin response (no 401/403/redirect oracle), proving the route does not admit to existing; collapsing the two arms must re-RED this @property assertion.
Green-by-inheritance once the issuance is_workspace_admin gate and resource_not_found_page() posture are wired on both legs.
steps.scenario_name: A non-admin cannot tell the issuance surface exists

steps.name: CSRF on both POST surfaces
criteria: Greens exactly one scenario: "Both submissions are refused without a valid security token".
A forged issuance POST without a valid double-submit token is refused by the shipped csrf_middleware before the handler runs and creates no invite (AC-03.9, NFR-6).

A forged accept POST without a valid token is likewise refused before the handler runs, creating no account and no consume; both new POST surfaces mount under the shipped double-submit layer with no exempt-path entry.
Green-by-inheritance once CSRF screening covers both /workspace/invites POST and the member accept POST.
steps.scenario_name: Both submissions are refused without a valid security token

steps.name: No secret leakage in logs
criteria: Greens exactly one scenario: "No invite signature or password ever appears in the logs" (@property).

After a full issue-plus-accept-plus-refusal cycle, the application logs contain no invite signature value and no submitted password; refusal reasons live in tracing keyed on invite_id only (AC-03.10, NFR-5).
Green-by-inheritance once the new issuance and member-accept handlers observe the tracing-keyed-on-invite_id discipline; the @property no-secret-leakage invariant is example-pinned at LAYER 3.
steps.scenario_name: No invite signature or password ever appears in the logs

steps.name: Password recovery: weak, mismatched, and minimum-length boundary on the member arm
criteria: Greens three scenarios: "A weak password is corrected inline and creates no account", "A mismatched confirmation is corrected inline and creates no account", and "A password exactly at the minimum length is accepted".

A password below the min-12 policy re-renders the set-password form with an inline error; check_password_policy runs before any tx opens, so the invite stays live and unconsumed and no account is created (AC-04.1, FR-8, NFR-4).
A confirmation that does not match the new password re-renders inline with no tx, no consume, and no account; the invite stays re-usable for a valid retry (AC-04.2).
A twelve-character password and matching confirmation is accepted by check_password_policy and the member account is created, confirming the policy is at-least-12 inclusive (AC-04.4, NFR-4).
Green-by-inheritance once the pre-consume check_password_policy and confirm-match guards on the member arm exist.
steps.scenario_name: A weak password is corrected inline and creates no account

steps.name: Issuance plus retry recovery: valid retry completes the join, blank email corrected inline
criteria: Greens two scenarios: "A valid retry on the same member invite after an error completes the join" and "A blank email on the issuance form is corrected inline".

After an inline password error on a still-live member invite, submitting a valid password and confirmation on the same invite completes the join: the member is created, signed in, and the invite is recorded used exactly once (AC-04.5, FR-8).
A blank or malformed email on the issuance form re-renders the form with an inline error and creates no invite, proving issuance inline email validation (AC-04.3, FR-3).

Green-by-inheritance once the member arm leaves the invite live on a recoverable error and the issuance email validation exists; the recoverability proof that an inline error strands nobody on a dead link.
steps.scenario_name: A valid retry on the same member invite after an error completes the join
